evidence: Cic. Or. 211: quae Graecī κόμματα et κῶλα nōminant, nōs rēctē incīsa et membra dīcimus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A limb, and so a member or clause of a sentence; a shorter phrase is incīsum. Traupman calls a main clause ōrātiō, which also means a whole sentence.

sources: Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 292.
